name: CrewOverview
facts: Evidence on demand: valid courses, expiry dates and who may fly what. Missing courses can be bought in the system.
overview: CrewOverview is the NGFT tool for the training, evidence and compliance of your crew in one place. It checks qualifications by crew member and position, each with evidence and expiry date. What each position needs is already set up and can be adjusted. Missing courses are bought right in the system and the certificate is created automatically; external certificates are uploaded and approved. The Pilot Qualification List shows who may fly what, including limitations and supervision. Crew and NPCT are reminded before a course expires. When the authority says “Show me the evidence”: you have everything ready.

de.overview: CrewOverview ist das NGFT-Tool für Training, Nachweise und Compliance Ihrer Crew an einem Ort. notes: Own external certificate: open the course list and use Upload beside the course, choose the file, enter Completion Date and Valid Until (or tick Certificate never expires), then Upload Certificate. The entry shows Awaiting approval.

A manager with Approve extern certificates opens Approve Courses, clicks the filename to review it, and can use the pencil to correct dates. Confirm the green thumb to approve or red thumb to decline. Both decisions are final in this workflow. A normal upload by a manager also waits for approval.

Managers with Bulk upload certificates can use One Certificate, Multiple Users after a shared training day, or One User, Multiple Certificates for one person. Select course(s) and member(s), supply the common file and dates, then Upload & Approve. These uploads count immediately. Company Administrator does not have this permission by default.

If courses or certificates seem to belong to the wrong company, check the company at the top. For a user working for multiple companies, use the three dots beside the company name, select the company, and wait for the page to reload.

Course appears unfinished: reopen it with the play arrow and check every Moodle component, including the feedback form where present. A composite training can have unfinished parts; expand it for progress. For a manager seeing stale red in Overview, use its refresh arrow to recalculate.

Missing course: ask the manager to check assigned roles, positions, operations and the company Relations Tree. Missing menu entries depend on permissions. To check a missing operation for a member, review Members > Properties, then aircraft assignment and the Allowed switch under Aircraft & Operation Authorization / Limitations.

Compliance of the crew: the reports show each member as a row and each requirement as a dot. Green is valid (Crew Overview shows the days remaining), orange is the buffer zone (expires within 3 months), red is expired or missing. Position Overview shows whether each member is complete for their position or operation. Crew Overview shows single courses and certificates.

The Pilot Qualification List (German: Berechtigungsliste) is the Aircraft Overview report: each row is a member and aircraft, each column an operation. A pilot may fly only if all required courses are green: the operation's own sign-off and all courses of the position. A blue ring on the dot means Under Supervision (only together with an experienced pilot). A dark disc means Limitations, for example Visibility > 8km. A ring with a disc means both. A click on the dot shows the details.
Evidence for an audit: every report can be saved as a picture or exported to Excel with the filters applied.

Yes. The required courses are in the system. Every e-learning course of a role or position can be bought with the cart icon in My Courses, or as a bundle with one click (refresher bundles cost less). Managers with the permission Buy courses for crew members can buy for a member. A bundle works as a subscription: the latest course is enrolled automatically every year, and the invoice is sent automatically. After completion the certificate is created automatically; only training done outside the system needs an uploaded certificate, which a manager approves.

Notification: the crew member and the NPCT get an e-mail when a certificate enters the buffer zone (usually 3 months before expiry), again 10 days before it expires and once more the day before. The status turns orange in CrewOverview at the same time.

The Relations Tree is the rulebook: it says which courses and certificates are required for which role, position, operation and aircraft. NGFT delivers the standard set according to EASA; the company can adjust it, down to the aircraft. A change applies to all members with that role or position. When a member gets a new position, the new requirements appear automatically.
